name: T-GATE (cached attention after a gate)
plain: After a sigma gate, it stops computing cross-attention, and optionally self-attention, reusing the last computed batch's cached result, averaged over cond and uncond once CFG is off. Past the gate the uncond pass is dropped and cfg becomes 1. This saves the attention calls while still running conv blocks. It replaces the transformer block forward.
math:
Cross: if σ<σ_gate and cached: n=attn2_cache; if only_cross or σ<σ_gate_attn1, n=mean of its chunks.
Self, only when only_cross is off: if σ<σ_gate_attn1 and cached: n=attn1_cache; if σ<σ_gate, n=mean of its chunks.
σ<σ_off (σ_gate if only_cross, else min of both gates): uncond=None, cfg=1. Gate σ from percent_to_sigma(start_at).

props.hook: Direct tb._forward or tb.forward assignment on BasicTransformerBlock instances (MethodType)
props.architectures: UNet BasicTransformerBlock; WeightFerry has its own

label: from code
surprise: It reassigns forward methods on the shared loaded model's blocks rather than object-patching them, so clones share it.

audit.note: TGate.py:45 reuses attn1 only when only_cross_attention is off, the opposite of 'if only cross ... also reuse attn1'. :101-103 and :49-50 average the cached result over its cond/uncond chunks; nothing keeps the first chunk. :197-202 also drops uncond and sets cfg 1 past the gate.
